headline: Approved Fall Town Meeting Warrant with $318,334 and $40,000 articles, and a Sunoco liquor license at 157 Worcester Providence Tpk.
summary: The board heard a consultant's study of the Fire Department. It recommends combining Stations 1 and 3 at one central location with 24/7 staff. The board also received an update on a cyber security attack on the town and schools.
decisions: Approved the September 8, 2026 Select Board minutes as amended, 5-0.
Approved a §15 Wine & Malt off premise and Common Victualer license for Sutton Express LLC dba Sunoco at 157 Worcester Providence Tpk., 5-0.
Appointed Anne Morris to the Council on Aging, term to expire June 30, 2029, 5-0.
Approved and signed the Fall Town Meeting Warrant, 5-0.

                                                                                             6:00 p.m. –  September 22, 2026                  
   HYBRID MEETING Roll Call vote taken:
Members in Attendance:
Chairperson Anderson, Vice Chair Ettamarna, Select members Limanek, Watkins and Spengler all present in person
Also attending in person: Town Manager Austin Cyganiewicz & Deb Jacques, secretary
Public Forum –  N/A
Select person Limanek motions to approve Select Board minutes from September 8, 2026 as amended, Select Watkins provides 
clarification on the amended minutes regarding the temperature requirement for special ed placement- Vice Chair Ettamarna seconds 
passes 5-0 with roll call vote- Limanek “aye” Watkins “aye”, Ettamarna “aye”, Spengler “aye” Anderson “aye”
*Public Hearing* Sutton Express LLC dba Sunoco 157 Worc. Prov. Tpk- §15 Wine & Malt off premise & Common Vic. as posted in 
the August 27, 2026 Millbury Sutton chronicle read into record by Select. Watkins- present is Atty. Kevin Quinlan and Manager of 
Record Vrushank Patel. Atty. Quinlan requests these licenses stating the new owner purchased in July 2026- there will be 2 coolers/6 
doors locked at all times. All workers will be TIP certified and there will be 2 employees at all times. This business owner owns 
several gas stations with liquor licenses in others towns within MA. Select Limanek asks for clarification with the existing store- the 
space seems small- will they be eliminating any of the current items for sale. Vrushank replies they have ordered new coolers for the 
beer & wine that will have locks on them. Jesse goes on to say Sutton has a strong history of enforcing compliance against underage 
drinking and at some point our Police Dept. will make sure they are following the laws. Vice Chair Ettamarna says there are a large 
number of teenagers with fake id’s- please have the staff be extra vigilant. A brief discussion involving the sale of Zyn products is 
discussed but they will not be selling this item. Select Watkins questions the cooler doors being locked- Vrushank replies yes they will
be locked. Hearing no further comments Vice Chair Ettamarna motions to close the Public Hearing- Select Limanek 2nds passes 5-0 
with roll call vote- Limanek “aye” Watkins “aye”, Ettamarna “aye”, Spengler “aye” Anderson “aye”. Vice Chair Ettamarna motions to
approve the request by Sutton Express LLC dba Sunoco- Manager of record Vrushank Patel for a §15 Wine & Malt Off premises 
liquor and Common Victualer license at 157 Worcester Providence Tpk. as posted in the August 27, 2026 Millbury Sutton Chronicle 
Select. Spengler 2nds - passes 5-0 with roll call vote- Limanek “aye” Watkins “aye”, Ettamarna “aye”, Spengler “aye” Anderson
“aye”
Appointment to Council on Aging- Anne Morris- Anne introduces herself to the board- she volunteers at the Sr. Center and would like
to add her voice to what goes on with the srs. in our town. After a brief discussion Select Watkins motions to appoint Anne Morris to 
the Council on Aging with a term to expire June 30, 2029 to fill the vacancy left by Gale Graves (Christine thanks Gale for her years 
of service) Select Limanek 2nds 5-0 roll call vote- Limanek “aye” Watkins “aye”, Ettamarna “aye”, Spengler “aye” Anderson “aye”
Presentation of Fire Dept. Study (Operations, Staffing, & facilities) - John Thompson with Mission CIT is present with PowerPoint 
(attached to final minutes). Also in person is Fire Chief Matt Belsito, Deputy Chief Robin Dresser and several of the Fire Dept. 
personnel and area Fire Chiefs. Town Manager Cyganiewicz states in the 2026 Capital Plan there was $45,000. Allocated for a Fire 
Staffing study. Mission CIT was the company chosen for study. Fire Chief Belsito states this was a long time coming this process 
started in Sept. 2025 and the results are a road map for years to come. The Fire Dept. has some pressing needs but we need a game 
plan. John Thompson introduces himself and says Sutton has a very good Fire Dept.- he appreciates and is impressed with all involved
in this study. John states they went back to the 2020 census figures for information- currently there are 4 full time staff and 25 on call
www.suttonma.gov
personnel (combination model) serving the rural, aging community with limited water infrastructure. Staffing challenges are evident 
with the volunteer numbers dropping from 32 to 27 members among the 3 stations. Hazard targets listed in the area are Route 146, 
Gilmore Dr., the schools, Unified and Purgatory Chasm. Workload calls for the 5 years in review were 3179 calls. Response 
performance did improve from 2023 at 11 min 41 seconds to 8 min. 8 seconds in 2025. Volunteers have been increasingly difficult to 
get as training is state regulated and takes 4-5 months of night and weekend classes. The review included detail of the 3 locations: #1- 
Headquarters- constrained by limited bay spaces, #2 Manchaug- most of the apparatus stored here with the weakest staffing (2on-call) 
& #3 Wilks- holds the largest call roster but storage is limited. This study supports consolidation of #1 & #3 but centralize the location
and support a 24/7 staff. In regards to funding the Fire Dept. budget for the past 4 years has overspent the overtime budget. It is 
recommended a 15-year Capital Planning horizon to address aging equipment & facilities that show deferred maintenance & little 
space for on-call members. In regards to the apparatus we should have fleet planning so vehicles do not exceed recommended service 
life- currently there are several vehicles that have exceeded service life.  In regards to Health & Wellness- it is important to support 
with programs and invest in equipment to fight against contamination, occupational cancer risks and behavioral needs. Key findings in
this study shows Suttons current ISO rating a Class 4 but opportunities to improve to a Class 3 through increased staffing. A stronger 
rating could lower insurance costs. In regards to Mutual Aid- Chief Belsito’ emphasis on the Depts. high response rate to commitment 
to Mutual Aid is nonnegotiable- The surrounding towns will be here for Sutton when needed. Mission CIT ended the presentation by 
saying Sutton is not in a crisis yet but we are at a strategic cross road. Select Limanek says this is the reality of the situation. When 
asked about the majority of call volume – it is between 8am-2pm. Recruitment is discussed- if any interest please contact the Fire 
Dept. Vice Chair Ettamarna questions the demand factors as well as the risk profiling/risk prevention. Jims priority is the wellbeing 
and safety of the 1st responders. Jim questions about billing the towns for Mutual Aid- Chief Belsito says no- Mutual Aid is reciprocal 
and they will respond when we need them. Select Watson thanks them for the comprehensive report. Christine asks if there is a 
reduction in graduates from the academy- John Thompson replies this is a national problem – volunteers are not what they use to be. 
Select Spengler questions the heavy load of training through the Mass Fire Academy- Chief Belsito states that is MA Law to attend 
and graduate from the academy. Dan asks if there was a centralized location could we combine the 3 stations? Chief Belsito replies 
no- we cannot give up Station 2. Chair Anderson says small towns rely on call firefighters- this model is no longer sustainable. No 
resident wants to see a long response time – we need to maintain our response time and get data that reflects the needs of the town. 
There is competition now for funding in town- Jonathan agrees that Mutual Aid is crucial – having each other’s backs. Regionalization
is the most sustainable to look at. Should we look more into Mutual Aid with agreements. Select Limanek says we have the road map- 
get things in motion. 
Approve and sign the Fall Town Meeting Warrant- Town Manager Cyganiewicz reviewed a few of the articles that were changed- 
Article 1 is to raise and appropriate a total of $318,334. Article 10 is to convey 38 Main St to resident that has been paying the taxes 
and article 11 appropriate $40,000. for water tank repairs at the Police Station. Select Spengler motions to approve & sign the Fall 
Town Meeting Warrant Select Limanek 2nds passes 5-0 with roll call vote- Limanek “aye” Watkins “aye”, Ettamarna “aye”, Spengler
“aye” Anderson “aye”.
Town Manager Update:
 The recent issue with the Cyber Security attack on the Town and schools was shared on our social media pages- we are 
working with 3rd party contractors.
 In regards to a question during the last Public Forum- there was a question about the status of an addendum approved by the 
Select Board & UGPG removing Lot 1 from the TIF agreement – that was approved by the EACCX at the June 24th meeting.
 Invitation from Amazon regarding air service (drones) in the northern sliver of Sutton there will be a meeting tomorrow – 
residents would have to opt in for this service.
 Sutton Leadership Group held a meeting last week to discuss the Fy2028 Budget. It was recommended at this time not to 
pursue a proposition 2 ½ override – and begin a strategic draw down of reserves to support operations for 1 year only and in 
the interim look at an override for FY2029. 
 CMRPC and Fire Chief Belsito began a discussion on a hazard mitigation plan- our plan expired in 2021.
Select Board Round Table
Select Limanek said the 9/11 25-year remembrance held at the Dudley Gendron was a very touching event- thankyou to those in 
attendance. Jesse thanks Chief Belsito for his invitation to attend Purgatory Chasm training held last week. It was an awesome event 
and the professionalism and dedication was evident of the participants.  The Sutton Food Pantry list of needs was read.
Vice Chair Ettamarna comments on how well done the 9/11 event at the legion was- Jim urges residents to watch the Tri Board 
meeting. 
Select Watkins mentions the recent Waters Farm Apple peeling event – also there will be on Sept. 26th a Manchaug 200th celebration 
held inside Manchaug Mill (6 Whitins Rd entrance) Mill 1 is still standing with adaptive uses. This will be 3-6pm. CMRPC- the state 
is having listening sessions for payment in lieu of taxes for state owned land. It will be in Sterling MA on the 24th or virtual Oct 6th 3-
4:30pm. Sutton has an assessed value of $25,213,800. FY26-27 of state owned land
